chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, who said:

A questioner asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who marries the daughter of a man, and the father of the concubine has wives and mothers of children. Is it permissible for him to marry any of the wives of the father of the concubine and the mothers of his children? And is it permissible for him to have any of his slaves from those who were his before the birth of the concubine or after? Or is that valid or not, except for the mother of the concubine who gave birth to her? He said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.أُمَّاتُ أَوْلَادٍ: Mothers of children (concubines who bore children)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to marry the relatives of a concubine's father in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the specific nuances of marriage and slavery within the context of concubinage (*ima'*), addressing whether a man may marry the female relatives of his concubine's father or retain ownership of her slaves acquired before or after her birth. The ruling of 'no harm' (*la ba'sa bihi*) indicates permissibility and validity, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential view that the kinship ties of the concubine do not prohibit marriage to her paternal female relatives, nor does the timing of slave acquisition invalidate ownership. This ruling underscores the flexibility of personal status laws in early Shia jurisprudence regarding non-marital sexual relations and their legal consequences.
